classification.difficultyReason: Relate equal gradients between square corners to the defining equal-ratio condition for geometric progression.

content.prompt:
The straight line below goes through a corner of three squares whose sides, in order, are $a$, $b$ and $c$. Show that $a$, $b$ and $c$ are in geometric progression.

Hint: Consider the gradient of the line.

spec.description: Three adjacent upright squares share a horizontal baseline. A rising straight line passes through all three top-left corners and meets the baseline left of the smallest square. Unshaded black outlines replace decorative cyan fills. Internal drawing coordinates preserve square shapes and corner incidence; they are not numerical givens.
spec.mathematics: Side lengths are a, b and c in left-to-right order. Horizontal separations between consecutive top-left corners are a and b; vertical separations are b-a and c-b.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied squares, straight line and side labels are visible; no proof or additional corner labels appear.

answer.short:
$\dfrac{b-a}{a}=\dfrac{c-b}{b}$, so $b^2=ac$ and $\dfrac{b}{a}=\dfrac{c}{b}$.

Equal gradients give equal consecutive ratios, so $a,b,c$ are in geometric progression.
answer.worked:
Let $A,B,C$ be the top-left corners of the squares with sides $a,b,c$, respectively. Since these corners lie on the same straight line, their gradients are equal.

$$\begin{align*}
m_{AB}&=m_{BC}\\
\frac{b-a}{a}&=\frac{c-b}{b}\\
b(b-a)&=a(c-b)\\
b^2-ab&=ac-ab\\
b^2&=ac\\
\frac{b}{a}&=\frac{c}{b}
\end{align*}$$

The consecutive ratios are equal, so $a,b,c$ are in geometric progression.
